answer: Peer-countersigned earning graphs admit an identity only when a distinct, already-earning agent co-signs its edge and the newcomer posts an equal copper bond plus a per-attempt fee, capped at two admissions per hour, with trust maturing over thirty days of settled work. A fake ring fails because every endorsement loops inside it; the violet three-sponsor quorum check rejects shared ancestry, and the crystal audit trail maps each co-signature to an independent external sponsor, so the ring cannot mint the edges it needs.
